title: Blue Activity uses bacteria to treat water in industrial cooling systems
abstract: The start-up combines microorganisms, water treatment chemistry, and continuous monitoring to reduce reliance on chemical biocides

title: Deconstructive Oxygenation of Cyclic Amines by Copper-Catalyzed C(sp3)–C(sp3) Bond Cleavage
abstract: Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed deconstructive oxygenation platform for the direct conversion of unstrained N-unsubstituted cyclic amines into versatile β-, γ-, and δ-aminoketones. The product diversity is achieved by adjusting the substituents at the β- or γ-position of cyclic amines that proceed through single or consecutive C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond cleavage, respectively. Following this method, we achieved skeletal modification of unstrained cyclic amines through ring contraction or atom replacement, leading to rapid structural diversification of cyclic amines.

title: Composite inflammatory, immune, and nutritional indices for predicting surgical site infection following spine surgery: a systematic review with narrative synthesis
abstract: BackgroundSurgical site infection (SSI) is an important complication after spine surgery, with a reported incidence of approximately 1%-4% and a substantial associated healthcare burden. Early identification of high-risk patients remains difficult. Composite indices derived from routine laboratory tests that integrate inflammatory, immune, and nutritional parameters may assist perioperative SSI risk stratification.MethodsThis systematic review with narrative synthesis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and was registered in PROSPERO (registration number blinded for…
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

title: A Combined Network Toxicology and Docking Study to Identify Putative Molecular Targets Linking Styrene Exposure to Atherosclerosis
abstract: BackgroundStyrene is a ubiquitous volatile organic compound linked to hematologic and vascular alterations; however, the molecular mechanisms connecting exposure to atherosclerosis remain poorly characterized.MethodsWe integrated peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomic profiles (GSE23746) with toxicogenomic data from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database, applying support vector machine recursive feature elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator machine learning algorithms to identify core targets at the styrene-atherosclerosis intersection.

title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
abstract: Predicting properties from coordinate–category data—sets of vectors paired with categorical information—is fundamental to computational science, manifesting in materials science as predicting formation energies or elastic moduli from crystal structures. While large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied to such tasks, optimal strategies for achieving reliable predictions remain elusive. Here we report fundamental limitations in LLM’s ability to learn from coordinate information in coordinate–category data. Through systematic experiments using synthetic datasets with tunable coordinate and category contributions, and a comprehensive benchmarking framework (MatText), we find that LLMs consistently fail to capture coordinate information while excelling at category patterns. This geometric blindness persists regardless of model size (up to 70 billion parameters), dataset scale (up to 2 × 10 6 structures) or text representation strategy. For material property prediction tasks dominated by structural effects, specialized geometric architectures consistently outperform LLMs, as evidenced by a clear ‘Graph Neural Network Language Model (GNN-LM) wall’ in performance benchmarks. Our analysis provides concrete guidelines for architecture selection in scientific machine learning.

title: Pathway Analysis of Testicular Dysfunction Microarray Data Implicates Alteration of ITGB1 Expression as a Key Determinant of Spermatogenic Impairment
abstract: Background: /Objectives: Primary, idiopathic, impaired spermatogenesis (IS) affects approximately 2% of men and can manifest as oligozoospermia or azoospermia. Methods: In order to gain insights into the genetic mechanisms involved, a systematic analysis of historical microarray data from testes with IS was conducted by first constructing a global map of signalling networks involving genes differentially expressed between IS and control testes (CT). The centrally located genes and their interacting genes were then extracted to create a sub-network representing the pathways active in IS.

title: Cation-Gated Interfacial Electrocatalysis: Mechanisms and Effects of Alkali and Alkaline Earth Metal Cations
abstract: Electrolyte cations, long considered inert charge-balancing species, are now recognized as active regulators of electrocatalytic interfaces. This review systematically examines alkali metal cations (Li+, Na+, K+, Rb+, Cs+) and alkaline earth metal cations (Mg2+, Ca2+, Sr2+, Ba2+) in five key reactions: hydrogen evolution/oxidation, oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, carbon dioxide reduction, and nitrate reduction.

title: Moa Foodtech turns the food industry’s trash into treasure using AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence speeds up ingredient discovery by suggesting new fermentation methods

title: Electrochemical Nitrogen Reduction to Ammonia with Mesoporous Molybdenum-Carbon Electrocatalysts in a Gas Diffusion Flow Cell
abstract: Commercialization of electrochemical nitrogen reduction (eNRR) is hindered by limited catalyst performance, the lack of scalable electrochemical cell architectures, and an incomplete understanding of performance-limiting processes. This work aims to address these challenges through a systematic investigation of catalyst composition and microstructure, device configuration, and reaction mechanisms.

title: Triacylglycerol fatty acid composition modulates ATGL regioselectivity and diacylglycerol output
abstract: Adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL) catalyses the first and rate-limiting step of intracellular triacylglycerol (TAG) hydrolysis, yielding diacylglycerol (DAG) and a free fatty acid (FA). The site of TAG cleavage determines the regioisomeric identity of the DAG product, with distinct consequences for downstream signalling and lipid metabolism. Here, we show that ATGL prefers specific fatty acyl chain lengths and that this preference contributes to its regioselectivity on heterogeneous TAG substrates. Structural modelling identified a substrate-binding pocket comprising a hydrophilic anchor and a hydrophobic tunnel whose dimensions favour long-chain FAs. Mass spectrometry-based analysis of DAG products generated by ATGL from defined TAG substrates revealed an intrinsic preference for terminal (sn-1/sn-3) ester bond cleavage. Acyl-chain compatibility modulated this preference, with poorly accommodated terminal chains increasing the relative contribution of sn-2 cleavage. Consequently, ATGL generated predominantly sn-2-retaining DAG species from heterogeneous TAG substrates containing long-chain fatty acyl chains, including substantial amounts of the sn-1,2-DAG regioisomer, which has not previously been associated with ATGL activity. These findings link the fatty acyl chain composition of TAGs to the DAG regioisomer profile generated by ATGL-mediated lipolysis and provide substrate-dependent parameters for more species-resolved models of lipid metabolism.

title: Low CAR affinity enhances T-cell synapse dynamics and activation
abstract: Low affinity chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) can clinically outperform high-affinity variants, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying affinity-dependent activity remain unclear. Here, we show that low CAR affinity enables faster CAR cluster motion, which is central to T-cell activation. We compared low-affinity CAT and high-affinity FMC63 CARs signaling at different stages of activation on supported lipid bilayers functionalized with defined CD19 densities. At low CAR expression on dense CD19 bilayers, low-affinity CAT CARs formed more mature and dynamic synapses, recruited ZAP70 more efficiently, and showed faster microcluster motion. These proximal signaling changes were accompanied by stronger calcium flux and increased NFAT nuclear translocation. Our data support a model in which weaker, lower-affinity CAR-antigen interactions promote receptor turnover, microcluster mobility, and signaling-adaptor recruitment, thereby enhancing downstream signal propagation. Our work provides a mechanistic basis for the superior functional performance reported for affinity-tuned CD19 CAR-T cells.

title: A Multiscale Theoretical Framework of Piezocatalysis
abstract: Piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical stimuli into chemical energy, holds significant promise for noninvasive medical therapies. In this process, ultrasonic frequency plays a dual role: it governs both the reaction rate and the electromechanical coupling efficiency, thereby serving as a critical bridge between microscopic and macroscopic physical processes. However, conventional theoretical models lack a multiscale description of coupled physical processes and thus fail to reveal how frequency dictates catalytic activity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Single-Water Microsolvation Promotes Proton Sharing in a Neutral Formic Acid–Ammonia Complex
abstract: Can single-water microsolvation promote proton sharing in a neutral acid–base complex? We address this question for formic acid–ammonia by isolating its monohydrated complex with broadband rotational spectroscopy and interpreting the resolved 14N hyperfine structure with calibrated high-level quantum chemistry. The observed complex is a single dominant HCOOH–NH3–H2O isomer with effective Cs symmetry, in which NH3 remains the primary proton acceptor, while water closes a cooperative hydrogen-bond cycle by accepting from NH3 and donating to the carbonyl oxygen. Rather than simply stabilizing the binary acid–base contact, this water molecule measurably increases its proton-sharing character. A resolved A/E tunneling pattern from NH3 internal rotation supplies the missing orientation needed to rotate the experimental 14N quadrupole tensor into the local ammonia frame, yielding an experimental χzz component and a quadrupole-derived Townes–Dailey ionicity of approximately 26%. High-level structures show the same directional response: O–H elongation, H···N contraction, and O···N contraction relative to HCOOH–NH3. Together, these results show that one water molecule can promote proton sharing in a neutral formic acid–ammonia complex without producing a separated ion pair.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
abstract: We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Leveraging traditional and advanced machine learning for comprehensive oncology data integration and outcome prediction
abstract: BackgroundOutcome prediction in neuro-oncology remains challenging due to heterogeneity in tumor biology, imaging characteristics, treatment response, and patient-specific clinical factors. Although molecular databases have advanced understanding of brain tumor biology, many datasets lack broader data necessary for generalizable predictive modeling. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being explored to integrate these heterogeneous data sources and support precision neuro-oncology.MethodsA narrative review was performed using PubMed and Embase to identify…

title: Light Ignites Lattice Oxygen in an Asymmetric Motif
abstract: Lattice-oxygen-mediated pathways bypass the energy-intensive steps that constrain adsorbate-mediated catalysis. Activating these pathways under mild conditions, however, means breaking metal–oxygen bonds that are, by design, strong. Asymmetric M1-O-M2 motifs, in which a bridging oxygen sits between two cations of different electronic character, decouple oxygen activation from oxygen release by distributing these functions across chemically distinct sites.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Scientists discover a hidden factor that can make or break chemical reactions
abstract: Researchers discovered a hidden factor that can determine whether chemical reactions succeed or fail, and then used it to boost the proportion of the desired product from 16% to 97%. By controlling acidity near electrodes, they developed a promising way to manufacture chemicals for plastics, medicines, and other products using oxygen and electricity instead of hazardous added oxidants.

title: Progress toward a Better BOCS: Systematic Coarse-Graining with Local Density Potentials
abstract: We introduce version 5.0 of the bottom-up open-source coarse-graining software (BOCS) package. BOCS employs the force-matching variational principle to parametrize potentials for coarse-grained (CG) models directly from atomically detailed simulations. BOCS version 5.0 significantly extends previous versions by treating potentials that depend upon the local density (LD) around each particle as well as potentials that depend upon the square gradient (SG) of this local density. We also describe a new package, PKG-BOCS, for simulating these potentials with LAMMPS. This software treats complex molecular topologies and provides considerable flexibility for defining the local density as well as the LD and SG potentials. We present numerical calculations that provide physical insight into these potentials and their dependence on the definition of the local density. These calculations also demonstrate the accuracy and reliability of our implementation. Finally, we demonstrate that LD potentials can improve the structural fidelity, thermodynamic properties, and transferability of CG models for water.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Synthesis of Large-area Two-Dimension Metal-Organic Framework Films via Chemical Vapour Deposition
abstract: Synthesizing uniform and large-are two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework (MOF) films directly on substrates is highly desirable and important for MOF-based electronics, but it still remains great challenge. Here, a simple chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth strategy with controllable-thickness and large-area capabilities has been developed to directly prepare them on substrates, in which 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand films pre-deposited on substrates react with copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac) 2 ) vapor, resulting the structure transformation from small…

title: Stabilization and Transformation of MXenes into Flexible and Thermal Oxidation-Resistant Non-van der Waals solids via Vapor-Phase Chemical Intercalation
abstract: Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) solids derived from MXenes exhibit attractive physical and chemical properties but are usually limited by the irreversible phase transformation of MXenes into rocksalt structures at high temperatures. Herein, we develop a vapor-phase chemical intercalation strategy mediated by high-vapor-pressure zinc (Zn) to efficiently stabilize the transition metals (Ti, Nb, and V) with unsaturated d-orbitals in MXenes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Chirally pinned flat bands, helical minibands, and bias-controlled topology of Jackiw-Rebbi states in a periodically modulated Dirac mass texture
abstract: Flat bands amplify interactions into correlated phases, and topological bound states are robust by principle; combining the two in a model that is both exactly analyzable and experimentally accessible is therefore especially desirable. Here we show that a square-lattice model with a slowly modulated Dirac mass texture, $m(x)=m+m_0\cos(2πx/L)$ with $L$ up to hundreds of sites, provides such a setting, without engineered geometries, lattice-scale textures, or long-range hoppings. Exact nesting reduces the problem, independently at each transverse momentum $k_y$, to a $1+1$ dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian with a position-dependent mass: every simple zero of $m(x)$ binds Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, and the two walls of a period form an effective Su-Schrieffer-Heeger ring. The model interpolates between a chirally pinned flat band at large $L$, a helical miniband whose nodes are enforced by a boundary phase of the ring, and a bias-dimerized regime in which the sign of the bias sets a winding number. A central result is that the miniband bandwidth is not a single scale: a max-min measurement conflates three widths of different origin, the helical height $W_{\rm JR}$ exponential in the period, the zone-edge upturn $W_{\rm edge}\propto L^{-2/3}$ dominating at large $L$, and a bias bump exponential in $L$, so the flat band is robust against bias in the thermodynamic limit. We analyze two lattice realizations, a two-orbital model with modulated inter-orbital hybridization and a single-orbital bond-order texture sharing the nodal physics while leaving the van Hove points gapless, and propose experiments on cold-atom superlattices, Kekule-ordered graphene, STM designer lattices, and microwave arrays.

title: Field-driven phase transition crossover in kagome antiferromagnet Mn$_{3-x}$Co$_x$Sn
abstract: Mn$_3$Sn exhibits a complex magnetic phase diagram with multiple symmetry-breaking phenomena. Minute electron doping at the Mn site breaks the kagome lattice symmetry in Mn$_3$Sn. In this work, we exploited this to tune the order of the magnetic phase transition using magnetocaloric effect in Mn$_{3-x}$Co$_x$Sn single crystals. Pristine Mn$_3$Sn shows metallic behaviour with a spin-reorientation transition at 278 K, which shifts to 175 K upon Co doping. Additionally, Co doping also induces a weak-ferromagnetic transition near $\approx 210$ K. The effect of Co doping results inverse to conventional magnetocaloric effect, with enhanced magnetic entropy change. Further, the scaled entropy change reveals a field-driven magnetic phase transition crossover from first order to second order in Mn$_{2.75}$Co$_{0.25}$Sn crystal. Based on experimental data, a new phase diagram is constructed, depicting the field evolution of various magnetic orders.

title: DNA nullomers as a statistical phenomenon
abstract: Nullomers are sequences absent from a certain genome. Due to their unexpected occurrence in short sequences, a hypothesis is that they are avoided for evolutionary reasons or because they might have lethal consequences on organisms. However, we present evidence that the occurrence and frequency of nullomers in genomes is expected as a stochastic consequence of uneven base pair combination distributions in the genetic code. This is done by artificially constructing whole genomes from statistics with a Markov chain model. The number of nullomers in these artificial genomes is in good agreement with the nullomer counts in reference genomes. Additionally, we investigated the nullomers of over 200 human genomes and found large deviations in the nullomers between individuals, further supporting the hypothesis that a vast majority of nullomers is very unlikely to have lethal effects.

title: Fluid shear magnitude, mechanical history and actin-sensitive coupling shape Piezo1 signalling
abstract: Mechanical forces shape cell behaviour, yet how Piezo1-associated responses encode force magnitude, recent mechanical history and cytoskeletal context under repeated fluid shear remains unclear. We combined defined fluid shear stress (FSS) with GenEPi, a genetically encoded reporter of Piezo1-proximal Ca2+ entry, in engineered XLGenEPi-HEK293T monolayers to resolve mechanically evoked responses at single-cell and population scales. GenEPi responses increased with FSS magnitude but showed diminishing response gain at higher shear. Repeated submaximal FSS produced history-dependent attenuation and reduced temporal coordination, with higher FSS accelerating the early phase of attenuation. Low-dose Latrunculin A, without significantly reducing bulk F-actin abundance, converted sustained FSS-evoked signalling into a brief, decay-dominated response while largely preserving peak responses to Yoda1. These findings show that Piezo1-associated signalling is shaped over minutes by force magnitude, recent mechanical history and actin-sensitive mechanical coupling, providing a quantitative framework for understanding mechanotransduction under sustained and repeated mechanical stimulation.

title: Functional dynamics of the eukaryotic RNA exosome upon complex formation
abstract: Rather than being static, proteins adopt multiple conformations and undergo dynamics on a wide range of timescales. Such conformational changes can be routinely probed by solution state NMR for protein sizes below 40 kDa and can be extended to large protein complexes with selective methyl-labeling strategies. Here, we expand the limit of methyl-NMR dynamics experiments to asymmetric protein complexes bigger than 300 kDa by investigating the inert core of the eukaryotic RNA exosome, Exo9. We demonstrate that isolated subunits are highly dynamic on the ms-s dynamics, which facilitates assembly. While ring subunits lose dynamics upon complex-formation, cap subunits and functional loops retain a large degree of flexibility as demonstrated by relaxation dispersion and chemical exchange saturation transfer experiments in the fully asymmetric Exo9 complex. Employing EPR spectroscopy we additionally revealed changes in the conformational ensemble and nanosecond dynamics of a spin-labeled functional loop region in the presence of the catalytic subunit Rrp44 and in response to substrate RNA binding. We thus demonstrate that an integrated NMR-EPR approach facilitates the characterization of functional dynamics that occur on a wide range of timescales in very large protein complexes.

abstract: These early-stage start-ups are developing chemistry that could reduce our reliance on fossil fuels, capture PFAS, and build better computers

title: Molecular Engineering of Fano Resonances for Enhanced Single-Molecule Thermoelectrics
abstract: Enhancing the thermoelectric power factor of single-molecule junctions requires simultaneously achieving high electrical conductance and thermopower, which are often mutually constrained. The sharp and asymmetric transmission features produced by Fano resonances offer a promising strategy for mitigating this trade-off. However, quantitative molecular structure–line-shape relationships linking molecular modifications to the resonance valley position and peak-valley energy width remain underexplored.

title: From metabolomes to phenotypes: predictive metabolomics across scales
abstract: Metabolomics has transformed plant biology by delivering high-resolution insights into the biochemical networks that govern growth, adaptation, and environmental responsiveness. The plant metabolome, encompassing both primary and specialised metabolites, acts as a dynamic interface between genotype and phenotype, capturing the interplay of intrinsic genetic regulation with extrinsic environmental cues. Significant technological progress has enabled increasingly comprehensive metabolic profiling, accelerating the discovery of novel natural products, the mapping of metabolic pathways, and the mechanistic dissection of stress responses. Beyond individual organisms, metabolomics is now being deployed at ecosystem scales: ecometabolomics and meta-metabolomics reveal the metabolic signatures of plant-microbe interactions, soil processes, and environmental gradients. Coupled with machine learning, predictive metabolomics further expands this scope by linking metabolic fingerprints to complex phenotypes such as yield and stress resistance, offering actionable opportunities for crop improvement and agroecosystem management. Nonetheless, analytical costs, sampling constraints, and limited data interoperability continue to restrict broader implementation. This review examines the opportunities and limitations of metabolomics across biological scales, from subcellular compartments to agroecosystems, and highlights its potential to connect molecular processes with ecosystem-level outcomes. Integrating metabolomics with imaging, volatilomics, and soil metabolomics will be essential for developing more sustainable and resilient agricultural systems under accelerating global change.

title: CloneOT: predicting clone-specific perturbation responses with lineage-supervised neural inverse optimal transport
abstract: Predicting single-cell perturbation responses requires mapping between two unpaired populations of cells measured before and after the perturbation. Optimal transport (OT) provides a principled framework for constructing such mappings by minimizing the transport cost, and neural OT methods (\textit{e.g.}, CellOT) have been employed for this prediction task. However, these methods rely on a fixed transport cost, typically the squared Euclidean distance. This cost may connect cells with the wrong responses. Lineage tracing provides the information needed to learn the cost, as heritable barcodes link the cells of the same clone before and after the perturbation. Here, we propose \CloneOT, a neural inverse OT method that learns both the transport cost and the transport map from partially lineage-traced single-cell datasets. \CloneOT\ represents the cost as a neural network. It learns the cost by minimizing the extra cost that the lineage adds to the optimal transport, so that the cheapest transport keeps the cells of each clone together. Our experiments demonstrate that \CloneOT\ recovers the correct transport on 2D datasets, while the squared Euclidean cost fails. Moreover, \CloneOT\ outperforms five baselines on 14 lineage-tracing perturbation scenarios of cancer cells, for both seen and unseen clones. Furthermore, we show that \CloneOT\ reveals the clone-specific transcriptional programs of drug-tolerant persister cells and forecasts the fate of each clone from its cells before treatment. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/poseidonchan/CloneOT.

title: Vibrational Fingerprints of Competing Structural and Polar Phases in CuInP2S6
abstract: Layered van der Waals CuInP2S6 crystals exhibit a rich sequence of temperature- and pressure-driven phase transitions, giving rise to multiple structural phases with distinct physical properties. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical efforts, unambiguous identification of these phases remains challenging because of their structural similarities and complex vibrational responses. In this work, we employ first-principles density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate the vibrational properties of the reference paraelectric C2/c and P-31c phases and their corresponding dynamically stable ferroelectric Cc and P31c phases, as well as the antiferroelectric P-1 and P-3 phases. From calculated phonon spectra and symmetry analysis, we determine the Raman- and infrared-active modes of each candidate structure and identify characteristic vibrational fingerprints that enable their phase determination through vibrational spectroscopy. Furthermore, using Porto notation, we establish polarization- and crystal-orientation-dependent Raman selection rules for different backscattering geometries and identify the modes that are expected to emerge or vanish under specific experimental configurations. Thus, our results provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for interpreting Raman and infrared measurements of CuInP2S6 and for reliably identifying its competing structural, ferroelectric, and antiferroelectric phases across temperature- and pressure-driven phase transitions.

title: An empirical model for deriving information on ion dynamics from $μ$SR data via the conventional Kubo-Toyabe function analysis
abstract: We present an empirical model that analytically relates the parameters of the extended Kubo-Toyabe (KT) function $G_z^{\rm EA}(t;Δ,ν_{\rm i},Q)$, which describes muon spin relaxation ($μ$SR) induced by jump diffusion of ions using the Edwards-Anderson parameter $Q$, to those of the conventional KT function $G_z^{\rm KT}(t;Δ_{\rm KT},ν_{\rm KT})$ that serves as an approximation of $G_z^{\rm EA}(t)$. The proposed formulae successfully reproduce the anomalous temperature dependences of the linewidth $Δ_{\rm KT}(T)$ and the fluctuation rate $ν_{\rm KT}(T)$ which are artifacts observed upon analyzing $μ$SR data on ion diffusion using $G_z^{\rm KT}(t)$. Applying this model to $Δ_{\rm KT}$ and $ν_{\rm KT}$ published in the literature of battery materials yields activation energy $E_{\rm i}$ and pre-exponential factor $ν_{\rm i0}$ in the Arrhenius equation for ion diffusion, $ν_{\rm i}(T)=ν_{\rm i0} e^{-E_{\rm i}/kT}$, that are in excellent agreement with those deduced using other techniques, transforming peculiar artifacts into a powerful diagnostic tool.

title: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution
abstract: Recent advances in self-improving LLM agents have demonstrated the potential of AI systems that drive their own intelligence. However, many domain-specific applications rely on specialized foundation models that possess strong domain expertise but remain dependent on human-designed improvements. Extending recursive self-improvement to these models presents a key challenge: as a specialist improves, the strategies used to advance it must also adapt. To address this challenge, we propose Heterogeneous Agentic CoEvolution (HACE), a framework that jointly evolves specialized foundation models and LLM agents through reciprocal learning. HACE improves the specialist through supervised learning while training the agent with on-policy reinforced self-training, guided by verified performance gains on the current specialist. The agent's exploration, in turn, informs subsequent specialist training, enabling both models to adapt to each other's progress. To sustain this reciprocal learning, HACE further employs evolutionary search to optimize their interaction harness, adapting how the models exchange information and select training experiences as their capabilities evolve. We evaluate HACE across three challenging domains: recommendation systems, protein function prediction in biology, and crystal stability prediction in material discovery. We show that HACE outperforms the evaluated self-improving methods on the primary task metrics across all three domains. These results shed light on heterogeneous coevolution as a universal approach to improving specialized foundation models through reciprocal interaction with a learning agent.

title: Nonrelativistic Optically-Induced Spin Torque in Noncollinear Magnets
abstract: Manipulating spin using contactless and non-invasive optical approaches is one of the forefront topic in the modern spintronic science and technology. Prior studies on optically-induced spin reorientation usually scales with spin-orbit coupling strength, setting a limitation on composing heavy elements. In this work, we extend such a limit into nonrelativistic regime by exploring noncollinear magnetic configuration. Using a general spin group-theoretical investigation, we show how the symmetric operators in both spin and lattice spaces control the spin torque and quantum geometry of Bloch wavefunction--including both quantum metric and Berry curvature. We describe their site-resolved spin symmetries and unravel their selection rules. Furthermore, we adopt a Kagomé lattice model and a realistic material family to showcase the local spin torque under light irradiation. Since the nonrelativistic spin splitting usually spans on the order of electron-volt, significantly larger than typical spin-orbit induced splitting, the nonrelativistic light-induced spin torque is concomitantly much stronger. This work extends the previous opto-spintronics from relativistic to nonrelativistic limit, significantly broadening its realization platform.

title: How the Classical Baseline Shapes Machine-Learning Speed Claims in Topology Optimization
abstract: Topology optimization places material in a design domain to optimize a structure's performance, such as its stiffness or heat conduction. Machine-learning methods often report large speed-ups over classical, non-learned optimization, but a slow classical code or a lower-quality learned design can exaggerate them. We re-ran released code for eight methods on one workstation and studied two in depth: Optimize Any Topology (OAT), a diffusion model that generates designs, and a graph-based neural optimizer. Replacing the classical code with an efficient implementation of the same algorithm cut these two methods' speed-ups by up to 20-fold. We then timed the classical code until its design was at least as stiff as the learned one; for OAT, we picked this point after the runs, which gives the classical code its best case. Published timings imply a 134x speed-up for OAT on a 256 x 256 grid; our matched single-design comparisons gave 1.5x to 3.5x. At matched stiffness, the graph-based optimizer was slower than the classical code in all six two-dimensional problems. Of the six other methods, two kept their advantage, one shrank, one reversed, and two were not comparable. In an exploratory audit, language models judged that 8 of 28 speed comparisons in randomly sampled, openly accessible articles lacked evidence of equal design quality; our own review counted 11, so the count depends on who judges. We provide a comparison procedure and a minimum report: classical code, hardware, design quality, what each timing includes, and data-generation and training costs.

title: Measuring higher-order bulk topology in a programmable quantum simulator
abstract: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. Crystalline higher-order topological insulators can extend this principle by hosting localized corner modes in two and higher dimensions. Although these boundary modes can be detected spectroscopically through the local density of states, determining the underlying bulk topology, for example through nested Wilson loops, remains an outstanding experimental challenge. Here we use up to 728 qubits in a superconducting analogue-digital quantum simulator to realize and probe a hierarchy of one-, two-, and three-dimensional topological insulators governed by effective tight-binding Hamiltonians. By reconstructing complex propagators from real-space measurements, we obtain complementary boundary and bulk characterizations: local densities of states reveal localized boundary modes, whereas experimentally reconstructed band projectors yield bulk topological invariants, culminating in a three-dimensional octupole moment extracted through third nested Wilson loops. These results establish a route to realizing, characterizing, and manipulating topologically protected states in programmable three-dimensional quantum matter.

title: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence-based and pathologist scoring of murine bile duct hyperplasia
abstract: Bile duct hyperplasia in rodents, caused by chemical cytotoxicity, bile flow interference, or aging, is traditionally assessed through time-consuming microscopic examination by pathologists. We developed a deep learning-based, artificial intelligence (AI) model for quick and accurate assessment of bile duct hyperplasia in mice. The study utilized 127 hematoxylin and eosin-stained, mouse liver whole-slide images (WSIs) digitized using Aperio scanners.

title: Phosphorylation of β-arrestins impacts recruitment to Parathyroid Hormone Receptor 1 (PTH1R) at the cell surface and endosomes
abstract: {beta}-arrestins 1 and 2 are intracellular adaptor proteins that regulate the subcellular localisation and signalling of GPCRs including Parathyroid Hormone Receptor 1 (PTH1R), which produces {beta}-arrestin-dependent signalling that may selectively stimulate bone anabolism. {beta}-arrestins can themselves be regulated by post-translational modifications including phosphorylation, which dictates the translocation and signalling of the few GPCRs studied in this context to date. We aimed to investigate whether phosphorylation of {beta}-arrestins modulates their subcellular translocation in response to PTH1R activation. Translocation of {beta}-arrestins to the plasma membrane and early endosomes was quantified using BRET biosensors and immunocytochemistry with high content analysis. Phosphoknockout or phosphomimetic mutations were introduced to previously demonstrated phosphorylation sites in {beta}-arrestins 1 and 2, initially in bulk to assess overall effects. Plasma membrane translocation was altered only subtly, whereas early endosome translocation was markedly reduced for both mutations but to a greater degree for the phosphomimetic. Contributions of individual or paired sites were assessed by restoration to wildtype from the bulk phosphomimetic mutants. Dual restoration of S13 and T275 in {beta}-arrestin 1, or the analogous sites in {beta}-arrestin 2, restored the greatest degrees of early endosomal translocation, with complete restoration for {beta}-arrestin 1 and partial for {beta}-arrestin 2. Restoration of other sites had minimal or no effect. Dephosphorylation therefore appears to be required for PTH1R-stimulated {beta}-arrestin early endosomal translocation, with different phosphorylation sites implicated than some other GPCRs. These findings raise the possibility of differential {beta}-arrestin regulation by distinct stimuli which may have implications in therapeutic targeting of {beta}-arrestin-dependent pathways.

title: RetroPlanner: Multi-Route Expansion and Multi-Objective Reasoning for LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning
abstract: Multi-step retrosynthesis planning is often considered solved once a route to purchasable starting materials is found, but such a route should also be practical in real-world chemistry. Recent LLM-based planners formulate this process as sequential decision-making over an AND-OR graph, yet typically expand a single molecule per turn and are optimized for solvability alone, leaving alternative routes uncompared across the multiple objectives that determine practicality before the search budget is committed. We introduce RetroPlanner, an LLM-based planner that jointly compares multiple routes to steer the search toward higher synthesizability, as measured by reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. RetroPlanner is trained to reason over chemical evidence: structural progress from the target molecule, bond changes and reaction classes, where candidate routes diverge from one another, and how they rank across multiple objectives. Experiments on multi-step retrosynthesis benchmarks demonstrate that RetroPlanner recovers more alternative routes than prior LLM-based planners while improving synthetic route quality and maintaining a high success rate.

title: Where are C&EN’s 10 Start-Ups to Watch now?
abstract: Some of our picks have raised billions, while others didn’t survive

title: Human Metalloenzymes Are Disproportionately Linked to Disease: The HEAM Structural Annotation Resource
abstract: Catalytic metal-binding sites are established drug targets for many human diseases, yet systematic study of how metal function relates to disease is limited by the lack of a resource combining structural localization of human metal-binding sites with catalytic annotation at scale. We introduce HEAM (the Human Enzymatic Annotation of Metalloproteins), a structurally annotated dataset of 1,933 human metalloenzymes and 1,171 non-catalytic metalloproteins. HEAM incorporates annotated metals into protein structures at their corresponding binding sites and classifies each site as catalytic or non-catalytic using the machine learning classifier MAHOMES II. HEAM more than quadruples the human site-level coverage of the largest prior metalloenzyme database. Using HEAM, we show that human metalloproteins are significantly enriched in KEGG disease pathways relative to the human proteome, and that metalloenzymes specifically are significantly enriched in ClinVar pathogenic variants -- a distinction obscured in prior, catalytically unresolved metalloprotein datasets. These pathogenic variants are concentrated in metabolic disorders, indicating that metabolic dysfunction is a substantial contributor to metalloenzyme-linked disease. By pairing 3D structural annotation with catalytic classification, HEAM provides both a foundation for structure-guided drug design against metal-binding sites and a resource for determining how catalytic and non-catalytic metal function contribute to human disease.

title: CLARA: Compound Library Active Learning with Reasoning Agents
abstract: Batch active learning for ligand discovery requires a recurring decision about whether to exploit high predicted affinity, reduce model uncertainty, or broaden chemical coverage. We test whether a language model can make this strategy-level decision while candidate ranking and label revelation remain controlled by a deterministic Gaussian-process environment. Across four protein targets, ten paired seeds, and a 360-compound assay budget, a GPT-5.6 Sol agent outperformed random sampling in all 40 matched campaigns.

title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics jointly captures molecular state, tissue morphology, and spatial organization, yet spatial-domain methods are typically compared only at late training checkpoints, obscuring differences in convergence efficiency. We introduce MP-MNCA, a morphology-prior masked neighbor cross-attention framework that preserves the full 3,000 dimensional highly-variable-gene representation while selectively routing molecular information across spatial neighbors, with histological similarity incorporated as a continuous attention prior under a self-supervised masked neighbor-contrastive objective. Across 12 heterogeneous human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) sections, MP-MNCA is evaluated against established spatial-domain baselines using both convergence trajectories and epoch-wise spatial-domain visualizations. Our results show that MP-MNCA (i) reaches coherent spatial-domain structure in substantially fewer training epochs, as reflected quantitatively by convergence curves and qualitatively by progressive spatial grids, and (ii) maintains strong clustering quality, achieving a mean peak refined ARI of 0.546 versus 0.549 for the strongest baseline (STAIG), while attaining the highest mean refined NMI of 0.657 versus 0.640. Moreover, MP-MNCA outperforms STAIG on 7 of 12 sections in ARI and 11 of 12 in NMI, demonstrating faster convergence without sacrificing spatial-domain quality.

title: Defining Thixotropy
abstract: Originally coined 100 years ago to represent a shear-reversible sol-gel transition, the range of the term "thixotropy" has gradually expanded to encompass time-dependent changes in viscosity. Since this risks confusing "thixotropy" with ordinary nonlinear viscoelastic behavior, in this work we seek simple, historically faithful, quantifiable, and experimentally testable definitions of "thixotropy" that avoid this confusion. By analysing both historical tradition and published experimental data, we arrive at three complementary definitions. Definition 0 provides an idealized, purely inelastic reference useful primarily for recognizing thixotropy in a constitutive equation. Definitions 1 and 2, which are more practical, require, respectively, unusually large strains to reach steady state, and unbounded growth of the material relaxation time during rest. Definition 1 can apply in either shear-rate or stress-controlled modes, with the latter encompassing the so-called "viscosity bifurcation." These criteria are tested across diverse materials that we identify as thixotropic based on their responses clearly exceeding their viscoelastic reference scales. The framework is deliberately phenomenological and does not require specific microscopic mechanisms, allowing diverse materials to be described within a common rheological language, as is typical for rheological terminology. We believe that these definitions provide a practical framework for assigning thixotropy a more definite place in rheological taxonomy.

title: A Low-Temperature Tool for Acousto-electric Detection
abstract: We have developed an apparatus for the measurement of the acousto-electric effect (AEE) from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperatures. The AEE is excited by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) for which a lithium niobate piezoelectric actuator is employed. A very low background noise level is realized through careful electrical and mechanical design of the setup. The validity of the setup is tested by measuring the AEE in heavily doped P-type and N-type silicon. The opposite sign of the AEE signal was seen for both samples, showing dependence of the signal on the type of charge carrier being dragged by acoustic waves. The signal showed quadratic dependence on the driving voltage, which is consistent with the AEE literature. Further, a temperature dependence of the AEE signal was measured, which exhibits a monotonic increase with a rise in temperature. The ability to probe the AEE in bulk samples at low temperatures makes this setup a promising tool to investigate the AEE and related phenomena in different materials at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Lipid diffusion enhanced by molecular motors
abstract: An experimental study of myosin I motors on a supported lipid membrane with a nematic actin filament layer is presented. The activities of myosin I motors re-organize the actin layer, in particular the morphology of +1/2 nematic defects. Data from single-particle tracking (SPT) of lipid molecules reveal two interesting features. First, the distribution of average lipid speed over a track shows two groups of lipids (high-speed and low-speed), and the proportion of lipids to be high-speed is higher in regions rich in actin.

title: Influence of Graphite on Lithiation-Induced Strain in Crystalline Silicon Anodes​
abstract: Silicon has attracted considerable attention as a next-generation anode material for lithium-ion batteries because of its high theoretical capacity. However, severe volume expansion and structural degradation during lithiation remain major barriers to practical application. In this study, we investigated the effect of graphite presence on the suppression of lithiation-induced strain in crystalline silicon using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.

title: Benzaldehyde Is the Redox Mediator for Aerobic C–N Cleavage in Epoxy Composite Recycling
abstract: Chemical methods are promising avenues to recycle fiber-reinforced polymer waste. Here, we reintroduce tripotassium phosphate-mediated benzyl alcohol conditions for epoxy cleavage. While these conditions were developed in 2008 for anhydride-cured epoxy cleavage and have been applied to amine-linked epoxy cleavage, no account has been made of why these conditions should work with the latter, or why air exposure appears critical for their success.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Luminescent copper(i) coordination clusters: structure-property relationships, transformation into hybrid functional materials, and emerging optoelectronic applications
abstract: Atomically precise luminescent copper(i) coordination clusters have emerged as a sustainable, earth-abundant, and structurally versatile class of materials, offering a compelling alternative to noble-metal (Au, Ag) luminophores. This review comprehensively addresses recent advances spanning the period 2020 to 2026 in the rational design, photophysical characterization, and functional hybridization of these clusters. We systematically discuss nuclearity control (Cu2 to Cu22), ligand engineering strategies, and the structure-property relationships that govern emission color and quantum yield, with particular emphasis on Cu⋯Cu metallophilic interactions, tetrahedral distortion parameter (Δθ), and ligand rigidity. The roles of metal to ligand charge transfer (MLCT), ligand to metal charge transfer (LMCT), cluster-centered (CC) transitions, and thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) are critically analyzed. Sonochemical synthesis is evaluated as a potentially useful laboratory-scale approach for accelerating nucleation and facilitating in situ hybridization; however, its scalability, passivation efficiency and ability to suppress aggregation-caused quenching remain to be demonstrated through matched comparisons with conventional routes. The review further explores the transformation of discrete Cu(i) clusters into advanced hybrid functional materials incorporating polymer matrices, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), oxide supports, and carbon-based scaffolds. Emerging applications in chemical sensing, TADF-based optoelectronics (Φ PL up to 99.9%, EQE >35%), and visible-light photocatalysis are critically evaluated. Challenges including Cu(i) oxidation susceptibility, ACQ, and synthetic scalability are addressed, and future directions including defect engineering, machine-learning-assisted design, and sonochemical hybridization are proposed.

title: Prediction of Creatinine from NIR Spectroscopy Using Chemometric and Deep Learning Models with Indirect Urea Estimation
abstract: Renal biomarker estimation is important for evaluating kidney health status. Traditional methods for determining creatinine and urea levels rely on chemical reagents and analytical instruments. This study explores an alternative, reagent-free approach for determining creatinine concentration and estimating urea levels in human plasma samples using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy, chemometrics, and artificial intelligence.

title: Development of a nanomedicine approach to improve the therapeutic index of bexarotene.
abstract: Bexarotene (BEX), a retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases and inflammatory conditions, including multiple sclerosis (MS). However, its broader clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, and dose-limiting adverse effects, most notably hypertriglyceridaemia. In this study, we investigated whether conjugation of BEX to dextrin, a biodegradable polysaccharide, could improve its physicochemical properties and therapeutic index.

title: Accurately Probing [Fe(CN)6] Defects in Prussian Blue Analogues
abstract: Prussian blue analogues AxM[Fe(CN)6]1–y·zH2O (A = Na, K, M = Fe, Mn) possess a rich crystal chemistry that allows their use as insertion materials for batteries, water treatment, and smart windows, among others, applications. Despite being simple in appearance, their synthesis is complex and often results in defective, nonstoichiometric materials. These defects can be of neutral charge, such as interstitial water molecules, or charged, such as A+ vacancies or [Fe(CN)6]n− vacancies, whose presence implies charge balance by the remaining transition metal centers.

title: MDCL: Multi-source Information Fusion and Collaborative Contrastive Learning for Inferring miRNA-Drug Sensitivity and Resistance Associations
abstract: A growing body of evidence indicates that microRNAs (miRNAs) play essential roles in cancer progression, therapy, and drug resistance. They are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutic targets for overcoming cancer drug resistance. However, existing computational methods for predicting miRNA-drug associations are often limited by sparse labeled associations, reliance on single-modality data, and insufficient ability to capture long-range dependencies in sequences.

title: Real-space obstruction control of the shift current in two-dimensional Quantum Spin Hall insulators
abstract: The search for materials exhibiting a large bulk photovoltaic effect has recently expanded to low-band-gap systems capable of operating in the infrared regime, with potential applications in optoelectronics. Among the microscopic mechanisms contributing to this phenomenon, the shift current is one of the dominant sources of photocurrent generation. Owing to its geometric origin, the shift current is not only determined by the optical transition probability but also by the real-space displacement associated with the optical excitation, making non-centrosymmetric materials with obstructed electronic wave functions particularly promising candidates. In this work, using a tight-binding model of a quantum spin Hall insulator on a triangular lattice, we investigate the nonlinear photocurrent across trivial, quantum spin Hall, and higher-order topological insulating phases. We show that obstructed topological phases exhibit a substantially enhanced shift-current response, despite the similar electronic band structure. We identify the origin of this enhancement in optical transitions between states belonging to distinct Wannier-center sectors, which allow for a large real-space displacement upon photoexcitation and, depending on the topological phase, control the sign of the shift current. Our results extend the search for controllable bulk photovoltaic effects to materials characterized by real-space electronic obstruction and identify indenene, a monolayer of In on SiC(0001), as a promising candidate for realizing this phenomenon.

title: Superconductivity from altermagnetic fluctuations: the crucial role of sublattice polarization
abstract: Unconventional superconductivity in correlated systems often appears in the vicinity of a magnetically ordered state. This situation is also relevant for altermagnets, characterized by a nonrelativistic spin-split electronic structure in the presence of Néel order. Many proposed altermagnetic candidates, however, never cross the magnetic instability. We study superconductivity arising from altermagnetic fluctuations in such systems and show that the sublattice polarization (SLP) of the normal-state bands plays a pivotal role in determining the superconducting state. SLP, an inherent property of altermagnetic band structures that persists even without magnetic order, prevents Cooper pairs from forming between different sublattices. This suppresses pairing mediated by the nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, which favors spin-singlet superconductivity, and leaves longer-range same-sublattice bonds dominant. When the next-nearest-neighbor exchange is ferromagnetic, as expected for frustration-free Néel order, this results in spin-triplet superconductivity. This mechanism is fundamentally different from that in altermagnets with long-range Néel order, where the spin-split Fermi surfaces favor equal-spin pairing. Finally, when longer-range interactions in the disordered phase instead favor singlet pairing, SLP leads to singlet states with characteristic properties distinct from nearest-neighbor pairing states.

title: Theoretical Investigation of Oxygen-Vacancy Diffusion in SrTiO$_3$ using Neural Network Potentials
abstract: Oxygen-vacancy formation and diffusion play important roles in determining the electronic and atomic transport properties of SrTiO$_3$ (STO). Accurate analysis of such point defects requires sufficiently large-scale and long-time molecular dynamics (MD) simulations; however, direct investigations of oxygen-vacancy dynamics using {\it ab initio} MD (AIMD) based on density functional theory (DFT) are limited to relatively small systems and short time scales because of their high computational cost. In this study, we develop a neural network potential (NNP) for pristine and oxygen-deficient STO using a reference dataset generated from AIMD simulations. The trained NNP model accurately reproduces the DFT reference energies, atomic forces, and virials for both pristine STO and STO containing an oxygen vacancy. The NNP also reproduces the supercell-size dependence of the total energies and oxygen-vacancy formation energies, including the formation energy extrapolated to the dilute limit. Large-scale and long-time MD simulations using the NNP (NNP-MD) are then performed to investigate oxygen-vacancy diffusion. The resulting oxygen-vacancy diffusion coefficients show substantially better agreement with experimental data than those obtained from conventional classical MD simulations. An Arrhenius analysis yields an oxygen-vacancy migration enthalpy of 0.64 eV, in close agreement with the experimental value of 0.67 eV. These results demonstrate that NNPs trained on first-principles data provide an accurate and computationally efficient framework for investigating defect formation and long-time vacancy transport in perovskite oxides.

title: Interlayer Registry Controls Polar Topology in Twisted Bilayer h-BN
abstract: Twisting van der Waals bilayers creates a moir'e stacking field with periodically varying local interlayer registry, enabling spatially patterned polarization. However, a systematic understanding of how this registry-controlled polar topology evolves with twist angle, temperature, and mechanical strain is still lacking. Here, using first-principles-trained deep-potential molecular dynamics simulations, we show that spatially varying interlayer registry governs the polarization texture and can be directly tuned by twist and relative layer deformation. As the twist angle decreases, the moir'e polarization texture evolves from compact, nearly circular vortex-like patterns to extended triangular AB/BA domains. This crossover arises from enhanced lattice relaxation at small twist angles, which expands low-energy, oppositely polarized AB/BA regions and confines in-plane polarization mainly to domain boundaries. Despite this reconstruction, the local in-plane winding remains tied to interlayer registry and persists up to 1000 K, indicating robust topology against thermal fluctuations. We further show that the mechanical response is dictated by whether deformation changes the relative registry: homogeneous deformation of both layers produces only weak distortions, whereas layer-selective deformation strongly reconstructs the moiré polarization texture. A mismatch-matrix registry-mapping model is developed to capture this response, explaining deformation-induced changes in vortex radii at larger twist angles and triangular-domain geometry at smaller twist angles. These results identify interlayer registry as the central control parameter for forming and tuning moir'e polar topology in twisted bilayer h-BN.

title: OctMole: Multiscale 3D Molecular Generation with Hierarchical Spatial Flows
abstract: Generating accurate 3D molecules requires jointly determining a variable number of atoms, their identities, and geometry across spatial scales: global shape emerges coarsely, whereas chemical bonds demand fine local precision. Existing atom-based diffusion and flow models operate largely at a single scale, while dense spatial fields become costly at high resolution. We introduce OctMole, a multiscale octree flow framework for 3D molecular generation. A hierarchical occupancy flow progressively resolves sparse molecular support from coarse to fine, and a joint atom flow assigns atom types and continuous in-cell offsets to occupied leaves. This decomposition combines efficient global structure with subcell geometric precision, while cell corruption improves robustness to generated support. On QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, OctMole achieves strong chemical, distributional, and geometric quality, with particularly clear gains over Uni-3DAR on GEOM-DRUG and substantial efficiency gains over dense 3D generation. As an additional capability, intermediate occupancy states and selected regions provide spatial conditioning without task-specific retraining, supporting multiscale shape conditioning, regional editing, linker generation, and shape interpolation. Code and pretrained checkpoints are available at https://github.com/octree-nn/octmole and https://huggingface.co/Disembo/octmole, respectively.

title: Characterizing and Mitigating Distributional Bias in Physics-Informed Generative Models
abstract: Physics-informed generative models augment a data-fitting objective with residual penalties that encourage physical constraints to hold in generated samples. However, improving constraint satisfaction need not improve fidelity to the data distribution. We study this conflict in residual-regularized diffusion models and identify two possible consequences. First, the same prediction error can incur different residual costs near different feasible states, preferring states with lower residual sensitivity (avoidance). Second, this preference can extend to feasible states outside the data support, where the residual also vanishes (leakage). Motivated by this analysis, we propose a data-anchored penalty that weights prediction errors by the residual Jacobian at the clean training sample and normalizes the resulting magnitude. This removes the incentive to relocate to less sensitive states without changing the model architecture or sampling procedure. Experiments on a controlled synthetic system, three PDE systems, and molecular transition-state generation with flow matching demonstrate the benefits of anchoring. Code is available at https://github.com/TanjaBien/anchored_diffusion.

title: Solubility of poorly soluble species in bulk and nanopores from grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling
abstract: Poorly soluble species can have mean populations below one in small systems such as nanopores. In this regime, the grand-potential minimum, which identifies the most probable particle number, differs from the ensemble-averaged solute loading. We use grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling (GCWLS) to calculate the density of states $Ω(N_\mathrm{A}, N_\mathrm{B})$ for a binary Lennard-Jones mixture of solute B in solvent A, both in bulk and in slit pores. One set of GCWLS simulations gives ensemble averages over a range of chemical potentials, whereas conventional grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation requires a separate simulation at each state point. Independent GCMC simulations confirm the GCWLS ensemble averages. The solvent number distribution is nearly Gaussian, whereas the dilute solute distribution is skewed and Poisson-like. The most probable solute number therefore lies below the ensemble-averaged loading $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle$ and is zero whenever $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle<1$. Reading the solute loading from the grand-potential minimum underestimates it and can falsely indicate that no solute is present. Defining the oversolubility as $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}=x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{conf}}/x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$, where $x_\mathrm{B}$ is the solute mole fraction, we find $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}\approx12$ in a pore of 3.5 particle diameters width when both wall interactions are repulsive. Adding wall-solute attraction moderately raises it to $\approx13$, whereas wall-solvent attraction lowers it to $\approx3.4$. This comparison shows that the wall-solvent interaction controls most of the enhancement. As the pore widens, $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}$ decreases toward unity. In bulk and in nanopores alike, the solubility of poorly soluble species should be obtained from ensemble averages rather than from grand-potential minima.

title: Emergence of Temporally Irreversible Hierarchical Solid Patterns through Information-Bearing Field Evolution and History-Dependent Growth Arrest
abstract: Patterns are widespread in natural and synthetic systems. Their formation is often interpreted through diffusion-driven instabilities or static geometric constructions. While successful in many contexts, these frameworks struggle to encode the spatiotemporal growth history of independently nucleated domains and their resulting collective behavior, including temporal asymmetry and hierarchical pattern formation with progressive solidification.

title: Solvent-Dipole Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from Biomass
abstract: 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media.
