abstract: Nature employs bottom-up strategies to create elastic materials from protein assemblies, yet transforming structural proteins from abundant agricultural byproducts into customizable bioelastomers remains challenging. Here, we develop a strategy to fabricate bioelastomers with tunable mechanics by co-assembling keratins from wool and feathers through acid-induced coacervation. Time-pH superposition rheology reveals that wool and feather protein coacervates share similar viscoelastic signatures regulated by pH, with relaxation timescales spanning several orders of magnitude.

title: Molecular Property Prediction with Well-Calibrated Uncertainties via Graph Neural Networks and Conformal Quantile Regression
abstract: Accurate predictive uncertainty quantification (pUQ) is critical for assessing chemical property predictions. Incorrect quantification could lead to costly synthesis and characterization of drug candidates destined to fail, or result in misguided environmental regulations. This work integrates Conformal Quantile Regression (CQR) with graph neural networks to achieve accurate molecular property prediction and well-calibrated predictive uncertainty quantification.

title: FRACTAL: A Ratiometric-based Fingerprinting Framework for Robust Spectral Classification and Ratio-based Spectroscopic Marker Discovery
abstract: Spectral classification is conventionally performed on band intensities, yet ratios between bands have long served as diagnostic indices in vibrational spectroscopy, from lipid-to-protein markers of membrane composition to amide ratios reporting protein secondary structure. Their use, however, has remained confined to a handful of expert-selected pairs, leaving most of the ratio information contained in a spectrum unexamined.

title: Structural Non-Identifiability of Photochemical Reaction Yields from Linear Optical Observables
abstract: Identical time-resolved and steady-state optical observables can correspond to different reaction quantum yields when reactive and non-reactive dark exits are not independently resolved. We formulate linear photochemical networks as stable input-output systems with kinetic matrix K, observation matrix B, and reaction output vector q. Complete integrated yields are Φobs = BRu and ΦR = q⊤Ru, where R = (−K)−1 is the cumulative residence-time matrix. Pulse-steady-state equivalence and common rate scaling are treated as auxiliary linear-system facts.

title: Revisiting Spin Contamination in Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory
abstract: Mixed reference spin-flip time-dependent density-functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) has achieved widespread adoption as a computational method for describing photochemistry beyond the Franck–Condon region, as it removes most of the spin contamination limiting previous spin-flip (SF-)TDDFT approaches. The C → V excitation space, in which an electron from a doubly occupied (closed) orbital is promoted to an unoccupied (virtual) orbital, remains spin-incomplete in MRSF-TDDFT.

title: Adsorption regime changes the information needed for data-driven metal–organic framework screening
abstract: How much fitting evidence, and which materials descriptors, are needed to prioritize porous materials? We analyze archived computational uptake labels for 279,010 metal–organic frameworks at four CO2/CH4 conditions (298 K). In retrospective experiments using target-informed example selection, each condition reaches at least 90% of its B = 1000 top-5% recall endpoint by B = 500. Local-chemistry RAC descriptors improve methane top-5% recall by 0.175 at 5.8 bar but only 0.039 at 65 bar, consistent with a pressure-dependent balance between chemical and geometric signals.

title: ARGUS: A Four-Signal Joint Model for H5N1 Neuraminidase Inhibitor Resistance Prediction
abstract: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are the primary antivirals against H5N1 influenza, yet resistance profiles at the structural level remain incompletely characterized. Phenotypic screening requires one to two weeks in biosafety level 3 containment; during an active spillover event, this timescale is incompatible with clinical decisions. We present ARGUS (Affinity-and Representation-Guided Unified Scoring), a learned joint model combining four independent structural signals into a unified resistance risk framework: molecular docking affinity, protein language model evolutionary likelihood…

title: Machine learning prediction of bismuth recovery from literature data: publication-grouped validation, anchored calibration and chemical interpretation
abstract: Machine learning models trained on published leaching data often report high accuracy from random splits that place runs of one study in both training and test sets. This study tested whether reported operating conditions can predict bismuth recovery for a study that the model has not seen. A data set of 485 runs from 82 sources was compiled across six unit operations; runs designed to retain bismuth, plate part of a bath or recover another metal were set aside, leaving 375 recovery runs from 72 studies.

title: Permutation-inversion insensitive comparison of three-dimensional molecular structures
abstract: We present a new approach to compare molecular geometries from a purely geometric perspective. The first step of our algorithm uses permutation-insensitive alignment of two molecules with a Gaussian-kernel-damped analog of the mean-squared deviation (MSD) between two structures. Using this procedure, we restore a proper atom-to-atom mapping between two structures. This circumvents the factorial growth of permutation sampling in root-MSD analysis by globally optimizing a nonlinear function to find the best overlay of the structures.

title: AriadneX: Unknown Crystalline Phase Discovery from Anomaly-Aware Unmixing of Powder X-Ray Diffraction Patterns
abstract: Accelerated materials discovery produces experimental characterization data at a scale that requires evaluation to assess the chemical outcomes. For example, high-throughput materials synthesis approaches generate large arrays of powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns from complex phase assemblages, in which signals from known and unknown products overlap. Identifying unknown crystalline phases still relies on expert assessment of unexplained reflections and does not scale with data generation.

title: Iron Tetraphenylporphyrin for Electrocatalytic AmmoniaOxidation in Solution and Carbon-Supported Films
BRACE: Bayesian Residual-covariance Adaptive Calibration for Multi-Endpoint ADMET Prediction
abstract: Deciding which ADMET assays to run on a compound requires a calibrated probability that it will pass each assay not yet measured, given those already run. A multi-task predictor supplies these via the cross-assay covariance of its prediction errors (residuals), but this covariance is usually estimated once, from historical data. It therefore misses correlations specific to a program’s chemical series (scaffolds) and knows nothing about assays unique to the program. With only hundreds to thousands of program compounds, we adapt this covariance rather than retrain the predictor.

title: Finding a small cytokine inside complex biological matrices using nanobody-functionalized plasmonic metasurfaces
abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a key inflammatory cytokine involved in numerous physiological and pathological processes, including cancer progression, fibrosis, and immune regulation. Rapid and label-free detection of IL-6 in complex biological environments is challenging due to its small size, which is overshadowed by the presence of large numbers of competing biomolecules. In this work, we develop a method to detect the spectroscopic signature of IL-6 in complex matrices using a nanobodyfunctionalized plasmonic metasurface that acts as a surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) sensor.

title: From Molecular Building Blocks to Corrugated Graphitic Carbon Nitride: Chemical Origins of Structural Preference and Electronic Diversity
Harnessing remote weak interactions for fine-tuning the catalytic activity of rotaxane-superbases
abstract: Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a distinct strategy for controlling molecular function by translating subtle differences in noncovalent interactions into changes in molecular conformation and reactivity. Here, we show that remote weak interactions can be harnessed to fine-tune the basicity and catalytic activity of mechanically interlocked secondary amines. To this end, we synthesized two bistable rotaxanes, featuring a primary ammonium/amine binding site and either a triazole or a methyltriazolium unit as the secondary binding site.

title: The Impact of Linker Disorder in Multivariate Metal-Organic Frameworks on Mechanical and Phonon Properties
abstract: While the reticular nature of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) allows incorporating highly symmetric building blocks, it also supports linker asymmetry and linker mixing within a single material. These imperfections impact both the framework structure and, crucially, its underlying physical properties. However, microscopic configurations of organic linkers are challenging to detect experimentally and we lack accurate atomistic models computationally.

title: Computational design and prioritization of database-absent small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist candidates from public bioactivity data
abstract: Public bioactivity data were used to construct a reproducible workflow for the computational prioritization of small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist candidates. Exact IC50, EC50, and Ki measurements were standardized, converted to pActivity, and deduplicated after structural exclusion of peptide-like records. The resulting dataset comprised 337 compounds and 155 Murcko scaffolds. Morgan fingerprints and physicochemical descriptors were evaluated using ridge regression, random forest, and XGBoost with scaffold-based validation.

title: Imitation and Accuracy in Automated Electronic-Structure Method Selection
Evaluation and Health Risk Analysis of Residual Pesticides in Some Cereal Crops in Mangu Market, Plateau State, Nigeria
Strategy for the activation of porous molecular crystals using organic vapors
abstract: Porous molecular crystals (PMCs), i.e., crystalline solids with permanent, virtual, or flexible porosity, are usually synthesized by crystallization from solution, with the solvated molecules included in the pores as guests. To use such crystals as porous materials, the guest molecules must be removed. Typically, thermal treatment is used to promote their desorption, but this method often leads to the loss of crystallinity and catastrophic collapse of the porous structures due to the weakness of the intermolecular interactions.

title: Confinement-Controlled Cluster Percolation Shifts the Widom Crossover in Supercritical Methane
abstract: Supercritical fluids undergo significant structural and dynamic changes near the Widom line, which separates gas-like and liquid-like regimes. These phenomena are well understood for bulk fluids, but their evolution under nanoscale confinement remains poorly understood. Using a Grand Canonical Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics simulation framework, we show that confinement of supercritical CH4 in clay slit nanopores shifts the Widom crossover to lower pressures, with the shift increasing as pore size decreases.

title: Absorption and Emission Spectra in Aqueous Solution with Coupled-Cluster Accuracy
abstract: Quantitative prediction of electronic spectra in water requires an accurate treatment of electronic excitation, nuclear structure, and state-specific solvation including effects from hydrogen bonding. Here, photoacids and photobases in aqueous solution are used as stringent test systems for statespecific embedded cluster reference interaction site model calculations combined with the iterative coupled cluster models CC2 and CC3.

title: Aggregation-Induced Polarization (AIP) of Racemic and Achiral Organic Molecules Leading to Asymmetric Elliptical Polarization Displaying Optical Rotation
abstract: Aggregation-induced polarization (AIP) was found to enable racemic and achiral molecules to show optical rotation in clear and transparent solutions. It also leads to the specific rotation of chiral molecules to be affected by their concentrations instead of being nearly consistent as documented in literature and textbooks. In this work, we examined AIP effect in a series of solutions containing small racemic, achiral and chiral molecules.

title: In Situ Ion-Exchange-Mediated Dynamic Nanointerface Reconfiguration for Polarity-Switchable Photoelectrochemical–Photothermal Biosensing
abstract: Conventional photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems typically rely on static semiconductor interfaces that merely translate biomolecular recognition into amplitude modulation of the pre-existing photocurrent, thus limiting their analytical robustness and self-validation capabilities. Herein, we report in situ ion-exchange-mediated dynamic nanointerface engineering to fabricate an analyte-programmed reconfigurable PEC–photothermal (PT) dual-mode biosensor for the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) assay.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Tumor-Activatable DNA Nanoengager That Orchestrates NK Receptor Clustering and Immune Checkpoint Blockage to Enhance Antitumor Cytotoxicity
abstract: Natural killer cell engagers (NKCEs) are promising immunotherapeutic agents for cancer treatment. However, their efficacy against solid tumors is severely limited by immune evasion mechanisms (mediated by the sialic acid–Siglec axis and PD-1/PD-L1 pathway), along with poor pharmacokinetics and off-target effects. Harnessing the precision and addressability of DNA origami, we engineered a tissue-specific, DNA origami-based, dual checkpoint-inhibiting NK synapse engager.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

title: Supercell-enabled inverse design of boundary-state dispersion for group-velocity control in pseudomagnetic phononic crystals
abstract: Topological boundary states offer a platform for guided-wave propagation within bulk bandgaps. Their propagation characteristics depend not only on the spectral extent of the states but also on their dispersion within the operating bandwidth. A nearly linear dispersion provides more uniform group velocity across frequency, whereas a reduced slope enables slow-wave propagation. Despite advances in inverse design of prescribed dispersion relations and topological dispersion tuning, application-oriented characteristics of boundary-state dispersion have rarely been direct inverse-design objectives. Here, we develop a supercell-enabled, surrogate-assisted framework for the inverse design of boundary-state dispersion in a phononic crystal with pseudomagnetic fields. Area-preserving anisotropic deformation shifts the local Dirac points, and independent variation of 21 rows within the supercell provides distributed control over the boundary-state branch. A constraint-preserving surrogate reconstructs the dispersion from an initial frequency and positive frequency increments, with first- and second-difference losses introduced to capture local slope and curvature. Coupled with a genetic algorithm, the framework targets two prescribed-bandwidth design tasks: highly linear dispersion and slow-wave dispersion. For the former, finite-element verification yields relative group-velocity variations of 0.142% to 1.183% over prescribed bandwidths of 4% to 6%. For slow-wave designs, mean group velocities of 190 to 385 m/s are obtained over bandwidths of 0.2% to 0.8% while satisfying a 5% group-velocity variation limit. These results establish boundary-state dispersion as a direct inverse-design target beyond conventional bandwidth optimization, opening a flexible route to group-velocity control through application-oriented dispersion engineering over prescribed relative bandwidths.

title: Peptide Assembly Design Algorithm: A User-Friendly Computational Tool for Discovering Amyloid-forming Peptides
abstract: Rational design of self-assembling peptides that form amyloid-like structures is challenging due to the vast combinatorial sequence space for amino acids. To address this challenge, we have developed the Peptide Assembly Design (PepAD) algorithm, a Monte Carlo-based method for designing self-assembling peptides based on pre-defined amyloid backbones. In this work, we introduce the user-friendly package, PepAD, to the research community (GitHub link: https://github.com/CarolHall-NCSU-CBE/PepAD-User-Friendly-Package).
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Stoichiometric Control in H 2 S-Mediated Nitrite Reduction at a Zn-site: Intercepting SNO 1− , SSNO 1− and HONO Intermediates
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) and nitrite participate in intertwined signaling chemistry, yet the factors governing product selectivity between nitric oxide (NO) and nitroxyl (HNO) and the underlying reaction pathways remain poorly defined. Here, we establish that reduction of a zinc-nitrite complex by H 2 S follows stoichiometry-dependent product selectivity. With 2 equiv of H 2 S, the reaction generates NO and HNO-derived nitrous oxide (N 2 O) trapped in 46.3% ± 2.1% and 19.7% ± 1.5%, yields, respectively.

title: Directional Prediction Errors Reveal Systematic Underprediction of Low-Pressure Carbon Dioxide Adsorption in Compact Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: A prediction residual has both magnitude and sign, yet materials-screening studies usually treat only its magnitude as informative. Here we show that residual sign localizes systematic underprediction of low-pressure carbon dioxide (CO2) adsorption to a compact, low-accessibility region of metalorganic-framework (MOF) descriptor space. We analyze 7,306 MOFs in a topology-held-out test set, keeping related framework topologies out of training. A one-sided 90% calibration defines the expected underprediction tail; critically, that tail is not distributed uniformly across materials space.

title: Programming Chemoselectivity in Aerobic Oxidation through Zr-MOF/Quinone Multicatalysis for Benzazole Synthesis
abstract: Selectivity control in aerobic oxidation reactions containing several oxidizable functional groups remains challenging. Herein, we show that the chemoselectivity of a Zr-MOF/quinone multicatalytic platform can be controlled through modulation of the organic redox co-catalyst. In contrast to previously reported Zr-MOF-808/(hydro)quinone combinations that promote direct heteroatom oxidation in anilines or thiols to yield the corresponding azoxy or disulfide compounds, Zr-MOF-808/1,8-dichloroanthraquinone unlocks a different reaction pathway to selectively oxidize primary alcohols in the…

title: CP-GFM-SGX: Topology-Aware Cyclic Peptide Generation and Design with Receptor-Conditioned Structural Evaluation and Experimental KRAS Affinity Optimization
abstract: Cyclic-peptide discovery requires molecular topology, atomic structure, receptor-associated evidence and computational decisions to remain consistent across a multistage workflow. We present CP-GFM-SGX, an all-atom generative AI model for cyclic-peptide design that integrates a topology-aware generative core with a Unified Evidence State Machine (UESM) to track candidate identity, chemical validity, provenance, typed failures and bounded computation. We evaluated three distinct aspects of the system.

title: UpKast: Method, Model, and Database for Large-Scale Cross-Solvent Determination of pKa Values
abstract: The acid dissociation constant, commonly written as p K a , plays a key role in chemistry. However, most p K a measurements have been conducted in only a handful of solvents, resulting in data scarcity for many relevant solvent systems. Herein, we introduce the UpKast-DB, which comprises of p K a estimates for around 3,000 acids and bases in 29 solvents. We constructed UpKast-DB using a quantum-chemical method that integrates solvation free energy calculations with experimental data.

title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters.

title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here.

title: Characterisation of thermostable CYP116B reductase domains as modular electron transfer units for redox biocatalysis
abstract: Electron transfer is a common bottleneck in redox biocatalysis. Here, we report the isolation of five cytochrome P450 reductase (CPR) domains from the thermophilic, self-sufficient CYP116B family. These enzymes have considerable industrial potential because their CPR and haem domains are naturally fused, yet the catalytic properties of the individual components remain poorly understood. EPR and UV–Vis spectroscopy confirmed the canonical FMN and [2Fe–2S] cofactors were present, although occupancy varied (FMN, 30–62%; [2Fe–2S], 10–33%).

title: De novo Rewriting DNA Identity into Functional RNA via Genetic Information Compiler
abstract: Genetic information is expressed through the molecular products encoded by DNA. Synthetic systems can regulate these outputs, but retain the original link between DNA identity and function. Re-engineering this link could assign new functions to existing DNA identities. Here we present a genetic information compiler (GIC) that converts selected double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) identities into user-defined RNA outputs. GIC exploits the nontrivial activity of λ exonuclease to interrogate dsDNA and release predefined activators.

title: Topology-Dependent Glass Formation Behavior in Poly[n]catenane Melts with Variable Ring Size and Chain Length
abstract: Poly[n]catenanes consist of cyclic subunits that are connected by mechanical bonds rather than covalent bonds, which gives them internal degrees of freedom and permanent topological constraints that are absent in conventional polymers. How these features affect the glass transition is not known. Here, we employ molecular dynamics simulations of the Kremer–Grest bead–spring model to determine the glass transition temperature, Tg, of poly[n]catenane melts with ring sizes of m = 8–50 beads and chain lengths of n = 5–40 rings.

title: Customizable Approach to Conformer Space Discretization using Torsion Angular Bin Strings (customTABS)
abstract: Conformational ensembles of small organic molecules are primarily determined by the rotameric states of their torsional or dihedral angles. The previously introduced concept of torsion angular bin strings (TABS) is a discrete vector representation of a molecule’s dihedral states, which therefore offer a quantitative description of such ensembles. Discretization of the torsional-angle space allows us to count distinct conformational states, giving an estimate of the upper limit of the expected conformational ensemble size (nTABS).

title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%.

title: Solvent Dynamics and Multiconfigurational Treatment Drive the Anomalous Stokes Shift of HINA
abstract: The 3-hydroxyisonicotinaldehyde (HINA) anion is one of the smallest known green-emissive fluorophores, yet the origin of its anomalously large Stokes shift (0.87 eV) remains unexplained. Given the well-established influence of the surrounding environment on the photophysical properties of fluorescent dyes, we examine its role in this shift by simulating the anion's absorption and emission spectra with four computational protocols that differ in configurational sampling, solvent treatment, and electronic-structure method.

title: Chromoselective Control for Aminoalkylation of CF3‑Alkenes through Low-Energy Photoredox Catalysis
abstract: Recent advances in chromoselective photoredox catalysis have demonstrated that light wavelength can serve as a powerful and orthogonal reaction parameter, enabling divergent reactivity from a single catalytic system. Building on recent advances in the sequential decarboxylative/defluorinative aminoalkylation of trifluoromethyl-substituted alkenes, we report a divergent, wavelength-dependent strategy for the site-selective functionalization of N-arylglycines.

title: Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
abstract: This work reports on a series of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-recruiting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) PROTACs based on a vorinostat-inspired HDAC inhibitor. Systematic variations of the VHL ligand, the exit vector, and the linker architecture revealed that longer, semi-rigid linkers promoted efficient HDAC6 degradation. Compounds 12-15 emerged as potent HDAC6 degraders, with 15 exhibiting a half-maximal degradation value of 26 nM with 12 showing particularly rapid degradation kinetics.

title: Free induction decay-detected high-field electron spin resonance for accurate monitoring highly polarized spin dynamics
Drug Molecular and Route Similarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented LLM Generation with Knowledge Graph for Semantic Reasoning
abstract: To address the inherent limitations of large language models (LLMs) in chemical synthesis—hallucinations, and low knowledge dense—this study presents a Knowledge Graph–enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (KG-RAG-LLM) with a multi-scale calculation of molecular and route similarity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that KG-RAG-LLM significantly mitigates hallucinations, increasing the proportion of concrete chemical information in generated responses to 39.52%–40.87%, drastically outperforming baseline LLMs and standard literature-based RAG pipelines in response completeness and…

title: Pathway Reweighting in DNA Reaction Networks Enables Adaptation to Environmental Pressures
abstract: Adaptive biochemical reaction networks must respond to environmental changes while maintaining function, yet synthetic networks typically rely on predefined pathways and stimulus–response relationships. Here, we introduce pathway reweighting as a strategy for adaptivity in DNA strand-displacement reaction networks. We design a splitting network in which two competing pathways connect a shared initial state to a common output. This allows environmental perturbations to redistribute reaction flux between the pathways while preserving overall network function.

title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates.

title: Density Functional Theory of Dion-Jacobson Double Perovskite Halides
abstract: First-principles density functional theory was used to study six (four unreported) hybrid layered double perovskites of the Dion-Jacobson A2MM ′′′ X8 family. All 6 compounds consist of organic diamines that bridge rock-saltordered inorganic octahedra, with Ag+ as the M ′ site and Bi+3/Sb+3 as the M′′′ site. Both aliphatic (1,3-diaminopropane [PDA], 1,4-diaminobutane [BDA], 1,8-diaminooctane [ODA]) and aromatic (para-phenylenediamine [PPDA]) spac-ers are investigated, revealing how composition affects the band gap character and magnitude.

title: Revealing Biomarkers and Candidate Drugs for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Using Bioinformatics and Deep Learning
abstract: BackgroundThere is a dearth of precise treatments capable of effectively decelerating the progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Consequently, there is an urgent necessity to discover novel potential biomarkers and rapidly translatable therapeutic drugs.MethodsThe GSE57148, GSE38974, and GSE173896 datasets were included in this study. Cell clustering and annotation were conducted via Seurat, and disease-related genes were screened through an integrated approach combining Scissor-based prioritization, differential expression profiling, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Subsequently, 12 machine learning algorithms were used to construct models and identify biomarkers. The mechanisms of immune microenvironment remodeling were analyzed through cell communication and pseudo-time series analysis. Furthermore, an in vitro COPD model was constructed based on BEAS-2B cells and validated by RT-qPCR. Finally, a deep learning model and molecular docking were utilized to conduct AI-driven drug repurposing screening targeting biomarkers.ResultsA total of 67 intersection genes were obtained. APRT, COX8A, EDF1 and RPL37 were identified as biomarkers for COPD. Further cell communication analysis revealed that CD4 naive T cells mediate immune microenvironment remodeling via the HLA-E-CD94/NKG2A inhibitory axis. Additionally, in vitro experiments confirmed that APRT, COX8A, and EDF1 were significantly underexpressed in the model group. Among these, EDF1 represented a previously unreported candidate biomarker in COPD and was therefore selected as a putative target for AI-driven drug repurposing. Deep learning and molecular docking targeting the novel target EDF1 identified several FDA - approved drugs with binding energies ≤ -5.0 kcal/mol. Among these drugs, doxycycline exhibited a stable binding conformation and strong binding activity with EDF1, indicating high potential for drug repurposing.ConclusionThis study identified four potential biomarkers for COPD and screened several candidate drugs targeting EDF1, providing new targets and translational strategies for the early diagnosis and precision treatment of COPD. EDF1 is a novel candidate target not previously reported in COPD; however, functional validation is required before it can be considered a therapeutic target.
venue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

title: Commit: Automated Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory for model-based pharmaceutical process development: a data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid model case study
abstract: In 2025, we introduced the Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory, an automated platform for crystallisation experimentation and Bayesian optimisation. However, the initial case study used a relatively simple three-parameter, single-objective optimisation problem. In this Commit paper, we extend the platform to a five-dimensional, multi-objective cooling-antisolvent crystallisation of lovastatin and benchmark data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid optimisation approaches. Sixteen screening experiments were followed by model-guided experiments targeting yield and particle size (D90).

title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. Each bead type was made from the previous one by the addition of one component. Batch experiments were carried out in water containing glitter, Cu(II), or both, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid without chitosan served as a control for the acid.

title: Electrochemical Capture of Microplastics via Reversible Metal Deposition in Aqueous Solutions
abstract: Microplastics are persistent aqueous contaminants for which effective removal strategies remain needed. Here, we investigate electrochemical deposition as a means of capturing suspended polystyrene (PS) particles. The purpose of this study is to understand the plausibility of electrochemical deposition as a means for removing microplastics from aqueous systems. The central hypothesis guiding this work is that ramified solid metallic deposits created during electrodeposition can mechanically capture plastic particles suspended in the liquid phase.

title: COSMO-RS-Based Theoretical Investigation of Equilibria in Protic Ionic Liquids
abstract: Ionic liquids have become an increasingly important field of research. A subgroup, protic ionic liquids, have been shown to be excellent solvents even for poorly soluble materials such as cellulose or polyamides. Still, the composition of such liquids, e.g., their ionicity and the nature of formed aggregates, is mostly unknown and experimental attempts to shed light on this have been mostly unsuccessful.

title: Cholesteric Liquid Crystals for Ultratrace PFAS Detection
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent, mobile water contaminants associated with adverse effects on human health and ecosystems. Current analytical methods require specialized instrumentation, complicating their on-site detection at ultratrace concentrations across distributed water infrastructures. Here we integrate fluorophilic partitioning and proton-responsive recognition within a cholesteric liquid crystal (CLC).

title: Building the Data Foundations for the Design and Discovery of Transition Metal Complexes
abstract: The unique chemistry of transition metal complexes (TMCs) enables several advanced technologies in diverse fields including renewable energies, medicine, and catalysis. Machine learning methods can accelerate their rational design but are bounded by limited dataset sizes, restricted chemical scopes, and insufficient quality. This Perspective surveys the current landscape of TMC datasets and investigates how they seek to address these challenges. The analysis focuses on the data curation processes as well as the scope of the properties provided, and their level of theory.

title: The role of membrane properties and environmental footprint in shaping the cost-climate optimal carbon capture processes
abstract: Membrane development for carbon capture is typically guided by CO2 permeability and CO2/N2 selectivity, although these properties alone cannot determine whether a material will deliver economically and environmentally favourable performance at scale. Herein, we develop a multi-criteria optimization framework that integrates a machine-learning surrogate model of a multi-stage membrane process with techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment.

title: Descriptor-Based Regression Analysis Enables the Discovery of Highly Selective Ligands for Palladium-Catalyzed Siloxycyclopropanation
abstract: A palladium-catalyzed siloxycyclopropanation of alkenes using acylsilanes as carbene precursors provides a distinctive catalytic approach to structurally diverse cyclopropanes through a siloxycarbene–palladium intermediate. Although the reaction scope and major mechanistic features have been established, the origin of its ligand-dependent diastereoselectivity has remained unclear, limiting the rational development of more selective catalysts.

title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO 2 -capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO 2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure.

title: Mechanistic basis of μ-opioid receptor allosteric modulation from molecular simulations
abstract: The μ-opioid receptor (μOR) is a central mediator of analgesia and opioid-induced adverse effects, yet the molecular basis by which allosteric modulators reshape receptor signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate all-atom molecular dynamics with unbinding kinetics simulations to resolve the mechanistic basis of positive and negative allosteric modulation of μOR.

title: Photocatalytic CO 2 Conversion Driven by UV Light Above 300 nm Using Ammonia as an Electron Donor
abstract: Efficient utilisation of solar UV light ( λ > 300 nm) is essential for practical photocatalytic CO 2 conversion. However, in conventional systems using water as an electron donor, slow water oxidation kinetics present a critical bottleneck that severely limits the CO production rate. Here, we demonstrate an efficient CO 2 conversion system that overcomes this kinetic limitation by employing ammonia as an alternative electron donor over Mg-doped SrTiO 3 loaded with Ag and Fe as dualcocatalysts (Ag–Fe/Mg–SrTiO 3 ).

title: Core-to-rim chemical zoning of a Paraíbatype tourmaline from Abulo, Ethiopia: Implications for origin determination
abstract: Copper-bearing tourmaline of Paraíba type is now mined at Abulo in southern Ethiopia. We report the core-to-rim characterisation of one colour-zoned crystal attributed to this locality, obtained in Bangkok in June 2026. A sawn slab about 12 mm across and 5 mm thick was e x t e n s i v e l y analysed by electron microprobe (113 points), LA-ICP-MS analysis (45 spots on two traverses and 58 isotopes, totaling 2,565 concentration values with silicon as internal standard and GSE and NIST 610 as external standards), LA-ICP-TOFMS imaging (13,500 measuring spots of 24 µm and 55 isotopes, totalling…

title: When Ethylene Meets Sulfur: Direct Synthesis of Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers
abstract: In inverse vulcanization chemistry, research has predominantly focused on multifunctional unsaturated comonomers to stabilize sulfur-rich structures, whereas the direct copolymerization of elemental sulfur with simple olefins has remained comparatively unexplored. Extending this concept to the simplest olefin, we report Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers (MinESC), synthesized through the direct reaction of gaseous ethylene with elemental sulfur via a base-mediated inverse vulcanization approach under mild conditions.

title: New Oxygen Sensor with Polyaniline Spin Probe and Low Frequency EPR (L-Band) Detection System
abstract: Our research demonstrates the potential of certain PANI samples to serve as sensitive and reliable spin probes for oxygen detection, while also highlighting the advantages of the low-frequency EPR technique. Compared to other methods of measuring oxygen concentration, the new sensor—based on a PANI spin probe and a low-frequency EPR detector—offers unique benefits: it ensures high sensitivity to changes in oxygen concentration and does not require direct contact between the EPR detector and the sensor itself (the polyaniline probe).

title: Conformational Heterogeneity and Local Electronic Structure in Wild-Type and Arctic Amyloid-Β42
abstract: Amyloid-𝛽 42 is a heterogeneous system, widely known as an intrinsically disordered protein, or IDP, sampling a variety of conformations. However, how ensemble redistribution affects the underlying local electronic structure remains less well understood. In this study, classical molecular dynamics simulations are combined with population-aware density functional theory and reduced active-space calculations to compare the LVFFA fragment of the wild-type and Arctic (E22G) variants.

title: Assessing the Limits of He Isotope Separation Under Confinement in Nanoporous Materials
abstract: Separation of helium isotopes is of interest owing to the critical importance and limited supply of helium-3 ( 3 He). Nanoporous materials offer a viable route for gas-phase isotope separation through either selective adsorption or quantum sieving. Here, to maximize the isotope selectivity of quantum sieving we propose coupling a strongly attracting open-metal site for He adsorption to a surrounding nanopore acting as a confining potential. We demonstrate that upon tightening the pore, the zero-point energy (ZPE) elevates up to a point where 3 He detaches while 4 He remains bound.

title: Defining the Catalytic Boundaries of N -Nitrosourea-Forming StzF/SznF and Related Metalloenzymes through Genome Mining and Mechanistic Analysis
abstract: Enzymatic N–N bond formation is a rare and chemically challenging transformation in natural product biosynthesis. The non-heme iron metalloenzyme SznF catalyzes the formation of the N -nitrosourea pharmacophore of streptozotocin via the coordinated action of a diiron heme-oxygenase-like (HDO) domain and a mononuclear iron cupin domain. Although recent computational studies have advanced mechanistic models for this transformation, the determinants governing substrate specificity within this enzyme family remain poorly understood.

title: A study of the valence shell photoionization dynamics following core level resonant excitation in imidazole
abstract: The photoionization and subsequent Auger decay dynamics of core-excited states in imidazole have been investigated at the carbon and nitrogen K-edges using linearly polarized synchrotron radiation. Ion yield measurements in the pre-edge regions were used to locate core-level transitions into either unoccupied valence or Rydberg states, and assignments were made through comparison with simulated spectra obtained using the RASPT2 method.

title: Enhanced Sodium Metal Anode Cycling Stability via an Organometallic Electrolyte Additive
abstract: Despite the high theoretical capacity of sodium metal anodes, practical application is limited by the general instability of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) leading to dendritic growth and capacity fade. Here we report that the dimolybdenum paddlewheel complex, Mo2(mea)4 (1, mea = 2-(2-methoxyethoxy)acetate), functions as an effective electrolyte additive for Na metal anodes at millimolar loadings, enabled by self-assembly on the anode surface upon formation of aggregates involving 1 and Na+.

title: Detection and Characterization of the Cosmological Neutrino Background by EPR Spectroscopy on Molecular Hydrino with Implications for Telecommunications
abstract: A hydrino atom, H(1/p) solved using a Maxwellian electrodynamics and relativistic mechanics, is atomic hydrogen with state energy En = -13.598/n2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is limited by the energy in the electric field of the proton to 126 whereafter the proton and electron decay. Electron transitions to hydrino states involve an initial non-radiative energy transfer to a catalyst that serves as an energy hole or sink of a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst such as HOH, a free or nascent water molecule.

title: Size-Controlled HgTe Nanocrystals Achieve Near-Unity Shortwave Infrared Emission
abstract: The near-infrared (NIR, 700-1000 nm) and short-wave infrared (SWIR, 1000-2000 nm) regions of light are privileged for optoelectronic applications due to the decreased scattering and diminished autofluorescence arising from the few natural chromophores which absorb or emit in these windows. We demonstrate a two-stage, size-resolved synthesis of spherical HgTe quantum dots (QDs) with narrowband photoluminescence tunable across the NIR and SWIR which combine exceptionally high photoluminescence quantum yields (QY > 80%), low polydispersity (<10%), and stability in air.

title: Mechanistic Classification of Multicatalysis
abstract: Multicatalysis combines two or more catalytic functions within a single reaction network and can unlock reactivity, selectivity, and synthetic efficiency that are difficult to achieve with an individual catalyst. Its mechanistic description, however, remains fragmented across partially overlapping terms such as tandem, relay, cooperative, synergistic, double-activation, and bifunctional catalysis, among others. Here, we propose a mechanism-first classification based on the relationship between catalytic functions and, specifically, on the catalytic ‘currency’ exchanged between them.

title: Substituent Effects on Anion Bonding and Disassembly of Hypervalent Iodine Macrocycles
abstract: A series of phenylalanine-derived hypervalent iodine-based macrocycles (HIMs) bearing electron donating and withdrawing substituents were prepared. The HIM associations with the anion of tetrabutylammonium chloride (TBA-Cl) were systematically investigated using binding isotherms generated via NMR spectroscopy. The association constants of the resulting I-Cl bond were found to linearly correlate with the electronic substituents via Hammett analysis. Electron-withdrawing substituents strengthened the I–Cl bond and disassembled the macrocycle more readily.

title: Understanding cell fate decisions with temporal attention
abstract: Understanding non-genetic determinants of cell fate is critical for developing and improving cancer therapies, as genetically identical cells can exhibit divergent outcomes under the same treatment conditions. In this work, we present a deep learning approach for cell fate prediction from raw long-term live-cell recordings of cancer cell populations under chemotherapeutic treatment. Our Transformer model is trained to predict cell fate directly from raw image sequences, without relying on predefined morphological or molecular features. Beyond classification, we introduce a comprehensive explainability framework for interpreting the temporal and morphological cues guiding the model's predictions. We demonstrate that prediction of cell outcomes is possible based on the video only, our model achieves balanced accuracy of 0.94 and an F1-score of 0.93. Attention and masking experiments further indicate that the signal predictive of the cell fate is not uniquely located in the final frames of a cell trajectory, as reliable predictions are possible up to 8 h before the event. Our analysis reveals distinct temporal distribution of predictive information in the mitotic and apoptotic sequences, as well as the role of cell morphology and p53 signaling in determining cell outcomes. Together, these findings demonstrate that attention-based temporal models enable accurate cell fate prediction while providing biologically interpretable insights into non-genetic determinants of cellular decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Prediction and Diagnosis of Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review evaluates evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for prediction and diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR). The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, through June 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies on AI/ML-based prediction or diagnosis techniques for FGR, Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) or Small for gestational age (SGA) fetuses. The prediction model risk of bias assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used to perform data extraction and risk of bias assessment.

title: Scalable Decoupling Contact and Configuration Spaces in a Quantum-Enabled Protein Folding Workflow
abstract: Near-term quantum devices remain constrained by limited qubit counts, noise, and shallow circuit depth, restricting their direct application to peptide folding. This work addresses this limitation through a hybrid quantum-classical framework that separates global contact-space exploration from local configuration-space refinement. The pipeline was evaluated on the p53 transactivation peptide. The peptide was encoded using discrete torsional states and Miyazawa-Jernigan contact potentials. Global conformational search was performed using simulated annealing, followed by fragment-level CVaR-based variational quantum eigensolver refinement. Overlapping fragments were stitched and reconstructed into three-dimensional backbone coordinates for structural comparison. Three independent simulated annealing restarts produced negative-energy conformers. The workflow identified a best global conformer at E = -3.70 MJ using simulated annealing. Fragment-level CVaR-VQE refinement generated 30 candidate conformers across three overlapping fragments, the best assembled conformer reaching E = -2.58 MJ after DP stitching and post-stitch refinement. In this trial, the classical SA solution outperformed the VQE-assembled structure and was selected as the final output. The final 65-atom model was successfully reconstructed, but full-backbone alignment against 1YCR yielded an RMSD of 4.65 angstrom, improving to 2.90 angstrom after trimmed alignment. Our work demonstrates a practical quantum-enabled peptide folding workflow for short, flexible peptides, but the present structural accuracy is insufficient for claims of native fold recovery. Its main value is as an auditable framework for testing NISQ-compatible folding strategies.

title: The role of a G-quadruplex structure in mediating the interactions of miR-1249-3p with the 3-UTR of the HNRNPK mRNA
abstract: Heterogenous nuclear riboprotein K (hnRNP K) is an important regulator of multiple signaling pathways involved in DNA repair and function whose expression has been found to be mis-regulated in many cancers and neurological diseases. The expression regulation of hnRNP K is not fully understood however it has been shown that the microRNA miR-1249-3p targets its mRNA 3-untranslated region (UTR), regulating its translation. In this study we identified a guanosine-rich sequence in the HNRNPK 3-UTR within the miR-1249-3p binding site that has the potential to form a G-quadruplex (GQ) structure.

title: High-throughput variant libraries and machine learning enable robust target-site selection for toehold-switch design in Detectrons
abstract: Programmable RNA sensors enable sequence-specific detection of RNA inputs for diagnostics, genetic circuit control, and multiplexed molecular readouts. Although readily programmable, their performance varies substantially with the target site selected within a transcript, making target-site selection a major challenge. Here, we report DeSTAR (Detectron Sensor TARget-site ranker), a machine-learning-assisted target-site ranking model for programmable RNA sensors. To train this model, we generated transcript-wide, single-nucleotide-resolution tiling sensor libraries across six diverse RNA targets, enabling generalization to be tested across transcripts rather than within a single RNA. In leave-one-transcript-out evaluation, DeSTAR's top-ranked sites were enriched for high-performing sensors in held-out transcripts, driven predominantly by interpretable sequence grammar in the sensor stem rather than transcript-specific patterns. Prospectively, on an unseen SARS-CoV-2 transcript, the model's top-ranked sites yielded working sensors roughly five-fold more often than random selection. These results support DeSTAR as a generalizable strategy for target-site selection in RNA sensors across transcripts.

title: The transformative power of artificial intelligence and machine learning in blood banking/transfusion medicine: A vein-to-vein approach from blood collection to transfusion services: On behalf of the AABB Foundation
abstract: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) are poised to transform transfusion medicine across the vein-to-vein continuum, from donor recruitment to recipient outcomes. Large datasets generated from millions of donations and transfusions create opportunities for predictive modeling, precision medicine, improved safety, and operational efficiency.

abstract: The company’s top candidate is designed to produce ammonia more efficiently through the Haber-Bosch process

abstract: Winners’ research areas include more-sustainable aquaculture biomass, autoimmune diseases, and human blood coagulation

title: Dual-mode detection of tetracyclines in animal-derived food samples based on MOF-on-MOF heterostructure fluorescent sensor coupled with machine learning algorithms
abstract: Tetracyclines (TCs) that accumulate in food enter the human body through the food chain, leading to drug resistance and health risks. This study synthesized a heterostructure fluorescent sensor, Zn-TCPP-MOF/NH2-MIL-53(Al) (abbreviated ZTA) for TCs detection. A dual-mode detection system was established by integrating fluorescence spectroscopy with machine learning algorithms and fluorescence imaging with YOLOv5, enabling precise detection of TCs.

title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens
abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Boltz-2, and Chai-1 each reproduced >50% of the Mac1 ligand poses to better than 2 Å root-mean-square deviation of experiment. Despite the potential for co-folding to describe protein conformational changes that stabilize ligand binding, we did not find that common conformational rearrangements, including peptide flip and a large loop opening, were recapitulated by the co-folding prediction. For AF3 and Chai-1, ligand pose prediction confidence weakly, but significantly, tracked experimental potency, while DOCK3.7 energies were only weakly correlated. Boltz-2 affinity predictions showed the strongest correlation with measured potency and, after calibration, achieved lower mean absolute error than a baseline predictor. We next assessed whether co-folding scores could rescore docking hit lists to distinguish true ligands from non-binders among hundreds of molecules prospectively experimentally tested against AmpC β-lactamase, the dopamine D4, and the σ2 receptors. AF3 ligand pose confidence values did not separate true ligands from high-scoring false positives as effectively as docking scores or Boltz-2 affinity predictions did. Taken together, the modest, but independent correlations of docking score and co-folding confidence or affinity suggest that integrating physics-based and deep-learning approaches may help with hit prioritization and subsequent optimization in structure-based ligand discovery.

title: PINPOINT enables non-destructive nanoscopic quality control of individual lipid nanoparticles and their mRNA cargo
abstract: Quality control of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) is central to development of mRNA therapeutics, yet ensemble measurements obscure critical heterogeneity in particle morphology and mRNA cargo loading. Here we introduce PINPOINT (Profiling Individual Nanoparticles with Precise Observation of INternalized Therapeutics), a single-particle nanoscopy platform for non-destructive, multiparametric profiling of preformulated LNP samples. Super-resolution imaging with Nile Red resolves size and morphology, while an optimized permeabilization strategy provides selective access to encapsulated mRNA without compromising LNP integrity. Single-particle fluorescence measurements, including RiboGreen and sequence-specific probes, enable quantification and validation of mRNA loading and identity. Comparative analyses of bare and encapsulated mRNA reveal kinetic and structural features, exposing heterogeneity masked by bulk assays. By integrating structural and molecular readouts at the single-particle level, PINPOINT establishes a quantitative framework for assessing of LNP composition and payload distribution, offering actionable insights for improving batch consistency and guiding the rational design of next-generation mRNA delivery systems.

title: Arsenic Impairs Critical Cellular Events of Human Cardiac Development Across Differentiation and Metabolic Maturation
abstract: Arsenic (As) is a widespread environmental contaminant, with exposure occurring primarily through contaminated food and water or cigarette smoke. Maternal exposure to As represents a significant risk factor for congenital heart disease in offspring. However, the mechanisms underlying As induced developmental cardiotoxicity remain poorly defined. Pluripotent stem cells provide an excellent platform for studying mechanisms of developmental toxicity. Embryoid bodies (EBs) derived from stem cells, can recapitulate many key events of early embryogenesis including germ layers specification. Human cardiomyocytes are derived from mesodermal progenitors. NKX2.5 governs cardiac specification and morphogenesis, and its mutation produces atrial and ventricular defects in humans. Using an NKX2.5 reporter stem cell line, we modeled mesoderm differentiation in EBs and cardiac induction in a 2D cardiomyocyte differentiation system. In an 8 day differentiation protocol, As (0.05 M; 3.75 ppb) significantly suppressed cardiomyocyte differentiation and cardiac induction. However, As increased mesodermal markers (HAND1, SNAI2, HOPX) gene expression. In contrast, cardiac specific genes, including NKX2.5, GATA4, Troponin T, and alpha actinin, were markedly downregulated in the presence of As. As also reduced expression of genes related to cardiac induction, fibroblast function, and vascular markers in the cardiac organoid model. As impaired cardiomyocyte maturation related gene expressions at concentrations without affecting cardiomyocyte proliferation. In a zebrafish model of early heart development, As increased heart rate and disrupted ion channel gene expression. In conclusion, As inhibits ESC differentiation into cardiomyocytes and disrupts cardiomyocyte maturation. Combining stem cell derived models with zebrafish exposure, this study illuminates adverse outcome pathways for As induced congenital heart defect.

title: Structural Basis for the Rational Design of UAMC-1110-Based FAP Radiopharmaceuticals
abstract: Radioligands targeting fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP) are promising tools for cancer diagnosis and therapy. However, the molecular binding mode of clinically established UAMC-1110-derived ligands such as FAPI-46 remains insufficiently characterized. To simplify synthesis while preserving key binding properties, we designed two novel derivatives - FAP-DD-101 (short aminoalkyl linker) and FAP-DD-102 (extended aminohexanoic acid spacer) - and evaluated them alongside FAPI-46 using molecular docking and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Across all derivatives, we identified a highly stable, energetically favorable charge-anchored binding mode, in which the 2-cyano-4,4-difluoropyrrolidine head anchors in a negatively charged subregion formed by Glu202, Glu203, and Glu204, mimicking the binding architecture observed in the FAP-linagliptin complex. MD trajectories confirmed that FAPI-46 and FAP-DD-101 maintain exceptional stability in this pose, with several non-anchored FAPI-46 trajectories spontaneously evolving toward engagement with this electrostatic subregion. For FAP-DD-102, linker elongation slightly reduced pose robustness, yet initial charge-anchored states still yielded superior average binding energies and vector stability compared to non-anchored poses. Overall, these findings elucidate the key structural determinants of FAP recognition, establishing a rational framework for designing synthetically accessible FAPI radiotracers with retained binding stability.

title: How Bacterial Growth-Phase Reshapes Synthetic Gene Circuit Function
abstract: The development of biological engineering tools have improved the ability to embed novel functions into living organisms. Concurrently, our understanding of the interface between synthetic genetic circuits and their host has accelerated in the past decade, enabling the development of context-aware predictive models. However, long-term circuit function remains difficult to predict when designs operate in field-relevant conditions.

title: Time-Resolved Physically Unclonable Functions Enabled by Solvent-Free Scalable Boron-Based Ultralong Phosphorescent Systems for Machine-Learning-Resilient Optical Encryption
abstract: Anti-counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time-resolved physically unclonable function (TR-PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high-dimensional temporal encoding.

title: Cation-Regulated Interfacial Proton Transfer for Enhanced C–C Coupling in Electrochemical CO Reduction
abstract: Electrochemical CO reduction reaction (CORR) on copper is a prototypical platform for studying C–C coupling toward multicarbon (C2+) products, yet the fundamental factors governing this process remain under debate. Particularly, how electrolyte composition regulates interfacial proton transfer and thereby governs C–C coupling pathways is still unclear. This paper describes the role of alkali metal cations in controlling C–C coupling in CORR by restructuring interfacial water and modulating proton transfer dynamics on Cu electrodes.

title: Structural basis for phosphorylation-induced inactivation of the rice ammonium transporter AMT1;1
abstract: Ammonium (NH4+) uptake and transport in plants are mediated by ammonium transporters (AMTs), which are tightly regulated by phosphorylation to prevent excess ammonium influx and toxic accumulation. However, the mechanism of phosphorylation-mediated inactivation is unique and remains unclear. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of the rice (Oryza sativa) ammonium transporter OsAMT1;1 in its wild-type and phosphomimetic variant T452D states. OsAMT1;1 forms a stable homotrimer, with conserved motifs affirming a shared transport mechanism within the AMT/MEP/Rh superfamily. Our structural analysis reveals that T452D phosphomimetic stabilizes an intracellular salt-bridge network and maintains the channel in a closed state, in which the ICL5 loop positions the hydrophobic plug residue Leu360 near the cytoplasmic exit to occlude the channel exit and abolish complementation capacity. Our findings elucidate phosphorylation-induced inactivation mechanism for the plant AMT1 subfamily, providing a structural paradigm for the post-translational regulation of nutrient uptake.

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
abstract: Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Stainless Steel vs Calcium Fluoride for biomedical Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: Raman spectroscopy (RS) has been shown to differentiate various disease states in tissue samples, yet the impact of sample substrate on spectral quality and downstream machine-learning (ML) performance is under-explored. We collected 960 spectra from 36 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded colonic specimens mounted in parallel on calcium fluoride ( CaF 2 ) and mirrored stainless-steel ( SS ) slides. Raw SS spectra were more intense than CaF 2 , and routine dewaxing left prominent paraffin peaks on CaF 2 that were largely absent on SS .

title: Ultrahigh Interfacial Thermal Conductance across GaN/BAs Interfaces via Atomic-Level Engineering
abstract: The integration of gallium nitride (GaN) with ultrahigh-thermal-conductivity boron arsenide (BAs) substrates represents a promising pathway for developing next-generation high-power devices. The heat dissipation capability of such integrated systems is fundamentally governed by thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces, and buffer layers such as Al2O3 have been widely adopted to accommodate lattice mismatch and facilitate heterointegration. However, the atomic-scale structural factors governing thermal transport across GaN/BAs interfaces remain unclear, limiting further improvements in interfacial thermal conductance. Herein, we propose an atomic-scale interfacial structural-uniformity strategy for engineering ultrahigh thermal conductance across GaN/BAs interfaces using molecular dynamics simulations augmented by machine-learning interatomic potentials. We show that interfacial structural uniformity plays a more important role than individual bond strength in determining thermal transport across the investigated GaN/BAs interfaces. For instance, the As-N-terminated coherent interface exhibits the highest interfacial structural uniformity and achieves an ultrahigh interfacial thermal conductance of approximately 2000 MW·m- 2·K- 1, representing a nearly eightfold enhancement over the experimentally reported Al2O3-mediated interface (250 MW·m-2·K-1). Finite-element analysis indicates that this atomic-scale optimization directly translates into device-scale performance, leading to a substantial improvement in overall heat dissipation efficiency. These findings suggest that engineering interfacial structural uniformity offers a promising strategy for achieving high-efficiency thermal management in next-generation high-power electronic devices.

title: Leveraging Cubenes to Access Highly Functionalized Fused Cubes
abstract: Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Tailored ZnO/Cellulose Separator Reconfigures Solvation Chemistry for Durable Magnesium Metal Batteries
abstract: Magnesium metal batteries represent highly promising candidates for sustainable energy storage owing to their extremely high volumetric capacity (3833 mAh cm–3), abundant raw materials, and intrinsic safety. However, their practical viability is severely impeded by uneven Mg deposition, catastrophic interfacial side reactions, and continuous gassing behavior driven by uncontrolled electrolyte decomposition.
